issues.description: download_and_untar.sh warns about missing unzip and bad args but continues execution instead of exiting
issues.detail: The unzip check echoes a message and falls through; the usage block prints help then proceeds with possibly unset $1. Missing archives also echo and exit 0, so the script can succeed with no data prepared. Add explicit exit 1 on missing prerequisites and bad args so failures surface immediately rather than propagating downstream.

issues.description: Transcript normalization is an unreadable, undocumented chain of sed substitutions over a partial character set
issues.detail: Seven chained sed calls inline strip individual Chinese punctuation marks with no stated target character class. Adding a new mark requires appending another pipe stage, and siblings like '！', '：', '；' silently survive. Lift the character map into a documented table or collapse into a single tr/sed with a character class, and assert the resulting text matches the intended set.

issues.description: README links to a config path that does not exist
issues.detail: README references ./conf/train/train_asr_branchformer_e24_amp.yaml but the file lives at ./conf/train_asr_branchformer_e24_amp.yaml. Anyone following the only reproduction doc hits a 404. Fix the link (or move the file) so the documentation matches the tree.

issues.description: data.sh deduplicates utt IDs and transcripts by independent sort -u and pastes them, risking row misalignment
issues.detail: The text file is assembled by pasting two separately sort -u'd streams without joining on the utterance key. The invariant that row i of utt_uttid corresponds to row i of transcripts.txt is unstated and unverified; any duplicate or missing key shifts rows and mis-pairs utterances with transcripts. Use join on the utt key instead.

issues.description: Unquoted command substitutions break paths with spaces
issues.detail: extract_dir=$(realpath $1) and zip_dir=$(realpath ${2:-$extract_dir}) are unquoted, so a download path containing a space silently word-splits. set -u does not catch this. Quote them as "$1" and "${2:-$extract_dir}".

issues.description: Hardcoded utterance counts inlined in data.sh complect dataset snapshot with verification logic
issues.detail: Magic numbers (22467, 3208, 6072, 29386, 38924) are embedded in the prep script, tying it to one TAL snapshot. If the dataset is re-released, the script fails opaquely. Extract expected counts to a manifest file the script consumes, or compute them from the transcripts.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a conventional ESPnet egs2 recipe addition that mostly follows the template, but the data-preparation shell scripts have real rigor gaps. download_and_untar.sh has broken guards that warn-and-continue on missing unzip, missing archives, and bad args, letting failures propagate silently. data.sh builds the text file by pasting two independently sort -u'd streams (a hidden alignment invariant) and normalizes transcripts via an unreadable chain of seven sed substitutions over an undocumented partial character set. The README links to a config path that doesn't exist. Fix the guards, factor the normalization, and correct the doc link before landing.
